Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Per our conversation, attaching a short recap and the SLO checklist we discussed so your team can confirm priorities. High-level items we captured: 

- Latency targets: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 250ms for single-turn generation (50-token average).
- Streaming: partial tokens should appear within 120-150ms for interactive flows.
- Throughput/concurrency: target steady-state 200 QPS with spikes to 400 for peak batch windows.
- Concurrency model: clients will open long-lived streaming connections (websocket/HTTP2).
- Fallbacks: ability to route to a slightly lower-cost model variant when Dedicated capacity is saturated.

Next steps we proposed on the call (MAP):
1) Redwood: run a 48-hour load test using your representative prompt set (we'll provide the harness).
2) FintechCo: confirm the representative prompt set + sample traffic profile by Wednesday 5/20.
3) Redwood: share SLO checklist + draft sizing for Dedicated pool + pricing.
4) Procurement: initiate PO / contract review after load test results and sizing.

Attached: SLO-Checklist-FintechCo-20260520.pdf (stub).

If the targets above are off, tell us now and we can recalibrate before running load tests.

Thanks —

Alex — quick technical follow-up / clarifications from the SE side.

On the call we flagged a few items I want to capture so the load test matches production behavior:

- Prompt set characteristics: average tokens per request ~50, 5% of requests include >256 tokens (long-poll downstream tasks). Please label any outliers so we can simulate tail behaviors.
- Warm cache expectation: we should expect a warm-KV-cache warmup window of ~10-15 minutes before p95 improves. We'll run both cold-start and warm-start passes.
- Batching policy: we plan to test with batching enabled (latency SLOs hold with batching up to 8-token groups) and with minimal batching for interactive flows.
- Streaming behavior: streaming flush interval can be tuned; baseline test will use 100ms flush to emulate your frontend. If you need sub-100ms, flag it — that increases resource needs.
- Concurrency model: we will simulate 200 sustained concurrent requests with short bursts to 400 QPS for 10-15 minutes.

Deliverables after load test:
- CSV of per-request latency histograms (attached after run).
- SLO pass/fail summary and suggested Dedicated pool size (GPU count + memory estimate).
- Suggested fallback model map and cost delta.

We can kick off the load test as soon as we get the traffic profile + prompt samples.

Ben Carter

Thanks Marissa / Ben —

This aligns with our internal expectations. A few clarifications from our side:

- Targets: p50 <= 75ms, p95 <= 225ms would be ideal for our UX team. If p95 at 250ms is required for batching, we need to understand the percentage of requests that will hit p95 vs p99.
- Streaming: our product team requires first-byte streaming under 120ms for chat UX. If you can demonstrate 100-120ms in the warm runs, we're comfortable.
- Concurrency: 200 sustained QPS is accurate. During market opens we can spike to +600 QPS for ~5 minutes. Can you simulate a 5-minute 600 QPS spike?
- Authentication: our IT team will need an architecture note on how token rotation and KMS integration work for Private deployments (cc'd IT).

We'll gather the prompt set and sample traffic CSV and share by EOD Wednesday 5/20. Procurement is looped for timing on PO — likely early June pending sizing and contract.

Also please include any assumptions about model variants (e.g., 8-bit quantization) that might affect latency profiles.
